statements.impact_statement: Trivy reports msgpack 1.1.2 only from inherited SBOM metadata with no filesystem package path. The final runtime filesystem contains msgpack 1.2.1, which fixes this advisory.
Trivy reports setuptools 70.3.0 only from inherited SBOM metadata with no filesystem package path. The final runtime filesystem contains setuptools 80.10.2, newer than the fixed 78.1.1 release.

The advisory is in LightningApp's Windows /api/v1/upload_file/ path. This image is Ubuntu Linux and launches only the RunPod serverless handler; no LightningApp HTTP service or upload endpoint is started.
The vulnerable /api/v1/state endpoint belongs to LightningApp. The production entrypoint is /opt/handler.py under RunPod serverless and never starts LightningApp or its state API.

The only load_from_checkpoint() call in the baked Hunyuan source tree is in hy3dpaint/train.py. The RunPod inference handler does not execute the training program and accepts no checkpoint or model path from requests.

The serverless request contract accepts an image and bounded scalar options only; it exposes no model/checkpoint path. Shape and paint assets are baked into the immutable image under fixed /models paths, so an adversary cannot supply the malicious torch model required by this advisory.

Model roots are fixed to baked local /models paths and the request schema has no repository, config, trust_remote_code, or model selector. Runtime sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, preventing attacker-controlled Hub repository loading.

The LightGlue remote-model attack requires an attacker-controlled repository/config. Hunyuan inference uses fixed baked local model roots, exposes no model repository input, and runs Hugging Face/Transformers in offline mode.
